newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Positive economic data from the United States energised Dutch bonds, powering them to a stronger close.
The figures suggested the U.S. economy was not growing too strongly, boosting up Treasuries, which pulled up Bund futures and guilder bond prices in their wake.
Dealers said prices fell in the wake of stronger than expected fourth quarter U.S. GDP growth but they quicly rebounded on news of moderate inflation data.
They said the bounce caught players by surprise.
"The market was basically short," said one dealer.

He said institutions remained largely absent from the guilder market, unsure about its direction, with professionals accounting for most business. "There's no cash trades. We're basically following Bunds," he said.
He also said the market was unswayed by Dutch figures showing a 3.2 percent rise in retail sales in 1996, stronger business confidence in December and lower capacity utilisation.
One trader said most people were expecting even lower prices after the GDP data but were caught by surprise.
"Instead of (falling), we saw some good position squaring," he said.
Another dealer noted that the 5.75 percent February 2007 Dutch state loan, widely considered to be the new 10-year benchmark in guilders, performed well in today's rally.
Those who bought the bonds in the recent tender, where yields averaged 5.64 percent compared with today's closing yield of 5.66 percent, are still nursing losses on this paper.
"It looks neutral to fair value now," he said.
